Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to read arbitrary files and thumbnails across all VFS mounts, leading to unauthorized information disclosure and potential exposure of sensitive configuration or data stored within the Foxel instance.

## Recommendation

- Identify all internet-facing instances of Foxel version 2.4.0 or earlier.
- Restrict access to the /api/fs/stream and /api/fs/thumb endpoints at the perimeter firewall or reverse proxy level until a vendor-supplied patch is applied.
- Implement monitoring on web server logs to detect unauthorized requests to the identified API endpoints originating from non-trusted IP addresses.

objects.name: macOS Persistence via Login Hook plist Modification
objects.description:
## Overview

The `com.apple.loginwindow` preferences domain supports the deprecated `LoginHook` and `LogoutHook` keys, which allow for the execution of arbitrary scripts or binaries with root privileges every time a user logs in or out. Adversaries leverage these keys by writing to the `com.apple.loginwindow.plist` file, typically located in `/var/root/Library/Preferences/`, `/Library/Preferences/`, or `~/Library/Preferences/`. This technique provides a mechanism for automatic execution during system boot or user login.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows for persistent execution of arbitrary code with root privileges upon every login or logout event on the affected macOS host.

## Recommendation

- Deploy file integrity monitoring to alert on any modification to `com.apple.loginwindow.plist` files across the environment.
- Review all existing `LoginHook` and `LogoutHook` configurations on high-value macOS hosts using `sudo plutil -p /var/root/Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow.plist`.
- Validate modifications against expected configuration management, backup, and system migration activity.
- Remove unauthorized hooks using `sudo defaults delete com.apple.loginwindow LoginHook`.

objects.name: Presenton: API authentication vulnerability (CVE-2026-120191)
objects.description: A weakness has been identified in Presenton versions up to 0.9.11-beta affecting unknown functionality of the component API. This issue results in missing authentication and can be initiated remotely. A public exploit is available. Upgrading to version 0.9.12-beta (patch 44c8a61122b21f17642d717b0c4d6f2c54c0f180) is recommended to resolve this issue.

objects.name: OpenCSG CSGHub: Authorization bypass via file resolve route (CVE-2026-120426)
objects.description:
## Overview
OpenCSG CSGHub versions through 2.6.0-ce are affected by an authorization bypass vulnerability in the unauthenticated file resolve route. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this by injecting a percent-encoded 'current_user' parameter into the file path. When processed, the application incorrectly forwards this parameter along with its internal server API key, causing the system to treat the request as authorized and allowing access to files within private models, code, or space repositories.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows for the unauthorized retrieval of sensitive data contained within private repositories, including source code, model weights, and other intellectual property hosted on the CSGHub instance.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade CSGHub to a patched version beyond 2.6.0-ce when available.
- Until patched, inspect web server access logs for anomalous requests to file resolution endpoints containing the 'current_user' parameter.
- Restrict access to CSGHub instances to internal networks or via VPN to reduce exposure to the public internet.

objects.name: Beta9: Build worker isolation deficiency (CVE-2026-120306)
objects.description: Beta9 worker pods perform image builds using Buildah with insufficient isolation. Tenant-provided shell commands are executed as RUN instructions within the worker, which shares PID, network, IPC, and user namespaces with the build worker container. The worker runs as UID 0 with CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE. Access to /proc/1/root allows the build process to interact with the worker's filesystem, which contains runc, buildah, and runsc binaries, Kubernetes service account tokens, and mounted host directories.

objects.name: Citrix NetScaler: AAA Service pre-authentication heap overflow (CVE-2026-8452)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-8452 is a memory corruption vulnerability in the Citrix NetScaler AAA service. The flaw is a heap overflow that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability is specifically reachable when the NetScaler appliance is configured to use SAML as either a Service Provider (SP) or an Identity Provider (IdP). A working exploit has been publicly disclosed, including a tool that deploys a webshell to the appliance.

## Attack Chain
1. Attacker identifies an internet-facing Citrix NetScaler appliance configured with SAML.
2. Attacker sends a crafted request to the AAA service endpoint to trigger a heap overflow.
3. Memory corruption allows for controlled execution flow redirection.
4. Attacker leverages the heap overflow to execute arbitrary shellcode.
5. Shellcode writes a PHP webshell to a predictable location (e.g., /vpn/theme/x.php).
6. Attacker interacts with the webshell to execute arbitrary system commands with root privileges.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the affected NetScaler appliance, potentially leading to full compromise of the device and persistent access.

## Recommendation
- Immediately patch all Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway instances to the versions identified by the vendor as non-vulnerable: NetScaler ADC/Gateway 13.1 (>= 13.1-63.18) and 14.1 (>= 14.1-72.61).
- Review network access controls to ensure the AAA service is not unnecessarily exposed to untrusted networks.
- Audit the web directory paths mentioned in the exploit (e.g., /vpn/theme/) for the presence of unauthorized files or scripts.

objects.name: TÜBİTAK BİLGEM eta-register: Missing authorization privilege escalation (CVE-2026-92886)
objects.description: CVE-2026-92886 identifies a Missing Authorization vulnerability in TÜBİTAK BİLGEM Software Technologies Research Institute eta-register. This vulnerability allows Privilege Escalation. This issue affects eta-register: from 2.0.8 before 2.0.9.

objects.name: macOS: Unauthorized screensaver configuration modification
objects.description:
## Overview

Adversaries can establish persistence on macOS by deploying a malicious screensaver (.saver) bundle and modifying the associated screensaver preference (plist) files. This forces the system to execute the malicious bundle whenever the screensaver activates. Detection focuses on identifying modifications to `com.apple.screensaver.*.plist` files performed by unsigned, untrusted, or common script-based processes.

## Attack Chain

1. Attacker gains initial access to the macOS host.
2. Attacker writes a malicious screensaver (.saver) bundle to a directory such as `~/Library/Screen Savers/`.
3. Attacker uses an untrusted process or script interpreter (e.g., `python`, `osascript`, `perl`) to modify the screensaver preference plist.
4. The system, upon user inactivity or manual activation, triggers the `ScreenSaverEngine`.
5. The screensaver engine loads the malicious .saver bundle.
6. The malicious bundle executes arbitrary code under the context of the active user session.

## Recommendation

- Deploy the provided detection logic to identify unauthorized modifications to screensaver preferences.
- Investigate any process modifying `com.apple.screensaver.*.plist` files that lacks a valid code signature or is a known script interpreter.
- Review the contents of `~/Library/Screen Savers/` and `/Library/Screen Savers/` for unexpected or unsigned .saver bundles.
- Verify that legitimate device management solutions or administrative scripts interacting with plist files are properly signed and identified as authorized.

objects.name: GPU pdma: Local privilege escalation (CVE-2026-20558)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-20558 describes a use-after-free vulnerability in the GPU pdma component. This allows for local privilege escalation without the need for additional execution privileges or user interaction. Patch ID ALPS11365070 (Issue ID: MSV-9547) has been identified for this issue.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows a local attacker to escalate their privileges.

objects.name: CyberStrikeAI: AI-orchestrated post-exploitation attacks
objects.description:
## Overview
The CyberStrikeAI framework is an open-source, Go-based penetration testing platform that integrates an LLM-driven orchestrator with a C2 server. Unlike traditional manual penetration testing tools, the LLM-orchestrator automatically determines the sequence of commands and technical steps required to fulfill high-level operator tasks. Victims identified include educational institutions in Africa and Latin America. The post-exploitation phase is highly automated, progressing from initial access via compromised SQL Server instances to full domain compromise with minimal human intervention.

## Attack Chain
1. Initial access via compromised SQL Server (version 16.0.1000).
2. Deployment of CyberStrikeAI C2 implant via webshell or existing access.
3. Establishment of persistence and local host reconnaissance (completed within 2 minutes).
4. Conduct of broad domain reconnaissance over approximately 5 hours.
5. Pause in activity for several days.
6. Final offensive stage including lateral movement via SMB and WMI, mass credential dumping, and database exfiltration (completed within 1 hour).

## Impact
Confirmed impact includes full domain compromise of educational institutions. The integration of LLMs into core attack operations enables rapid execution of technical tasks that traditionally required significant manual effort, drastically reducing the time required for lateral movement and data exfiltration.

## Recommendation
- Hunt for the presence of the 'X-Implant-Token' custom HTTP header in network traffic, as this is a consistent indicator of CyberStrikeAI C2 communication.
- Audit SQL Server environments (version 16.0.1000 and others) for unauthorized process execution, specifically looking for 'sqlservr.exe' spawning suspicious child processes (e.g., cmd.exe, powershell.exe).
- Monitor for unexpected WMI and SMB traffic patterns originating from database servers, which may indicate lateral movement.
- Implement memory scanning for Go-based implants that exhibit the specific build metadata patterns described by the framework.

objects.name: Videostrong Technology x.cpe Botnet
objects.description:
## Overview

Google’s Threat Intelligence Group identified and disrupted a large-scale botnet known as x.cpe, affecting more than 1.3 million Google-certified Android TV devices. The operation was attributed to Shenzhen-based manufacturer Videostrong Technology, which leveraged a pre-installed backdoor to remotely push malicious modules after device deployment. The malware transformed infected hardware into nodes for residential proxy networks, ad fraud schemes, and local network reconnaissance tools.

## Attack Chain

1. Supply Chain Compromise: Videostrong Technology pre-installs a stub application (com.oemservice) on Android TV hardware during manufacturing.
2. Initial Provisioning: The device is sold and set up by the end-user, connecting to the internet.
3. C2 Beaconing: The stub application initiates contact with attacker-controlled command-and-control servers.
4. Defense Evasion: The stub application disables Google Play Protect to prevent the detection of subsequent malicious payload installation.
5. Payload Deployment: The operator remotely installs modular malware payloads via system-level permissions granted to the stub application.
6. Malicious Execution: Modules execute unauthorized tasks including residential proxy traffic routing, ad fraud, and lateral network probing.

## Impact

Over 1.4 million devices were confirmed to be infected, with significant concentrations in Brazil, Malaysia, Iraq, Mexico, and Taiwan, and thousands of affected devices across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Canada. The botnet allowed operators to capture device screens, execute terminal commands, and probe local network infrastructure.

## Recommendation

* Inventory all Android TV devices within the corporate network, specifically identifying MECOOL-branded and white-label hardware manufactured by Videostrong Technology.
* Monitor network traffic for anomalies originating from Android TV devices, particularly high volumes of outbound traffic characteristic of residential proxy activity.
* Restrict internal network access for IoT and media streaming devices by isolating them in a dedicated VLAN with strictly enforced egress filtering.
* Implement device management policies that prohibit the use of unmanaged, consumer-grade Android TV hardware for accessing sensitive corporate resources.

objects.name: TP-Link Archer AX17: Authenticated OS command injection (CVE-2026-9151)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-9151 is an authenticated OS command injection vulnerability in the Archer AX17 v1 VPN client import functionality. The issue arises because the profile description field is insufficiently sanitized and later processed by system commands (`grep` and `sed`) running with root privileges. An authenticated administrative session from the LAN is required to exploit this.

## Attack Chain
1. Attacker establishes an authenticated administrative session on the LAN.
2. Attacker triggers the VPN client import functionality on the router.
3. Attacker submits a crafted OpenVPN profile description containing a payload using backticks and `${IFS}` to bypass input filtering (e.g., `` `sleep${IFS}1` ``).
4. The router stores the malicious string as a filename in `/etc/openvpn/.ovpn`.
5. The application writes the path to `/tmp/ovpn_curr_edit`.
6. The web server executes `grep` and `sed` commands using the unquoted path from `/tmp/ovpn_curr_edit`.
7. The system shell interprets the injected backticks as commands, executing the payload with root privileges.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows for full command execution on the router as the root user, potentially leading to a complete compromise of the network device.

## Recommendation
- Update Archer AX17 v1 firmware to version 1.5.0 Build 20260605 or later.
- Limit administrative access to the router web interface to trusted management subnets or hardened endpoints to mitigate the risk of an attacker gaining the required administrative session.
- Audit logs for unexpected administrative logins or configuration changes on network devices.

objects.name: Android November 2026 Security Updates
objects.description:
## Overview

Google has released security updates for Android for November 2026, addressing over 200 vulnerabilities, including more than two dozen critical-severity issues. The updates are split into two patch levels: 2026-11-01 and 2026-11-05. The most severe vulnerability is CVE-2026-58868, a critical-severity remote code execution (RCE) flaw in the Android Framework that does not require user interaction or elevated privileges. Additional critical vulnerabilities were addressed in System, Bluetooth, pKVM, HID, and various third-party vendor components.

## Impact

Successful exploitation of the identified vulnerabilities, particularly CVE-2026-58868, could allow an unauthenticated attacker to achieve remote code execution on affected Android devices without requiring user interaction.

## Recommendation

- Prioritize the deployment of the 2026-11-05 security patch level across all organizational Android, Android XR, and Wear OS devices.
- Verify that mobile device management (MDM) policies enforce the latest available security patch level for all corporate-managed handsets.
- Monitor for unauthorized or anomalous system process behavior on mobile endpoints, as the vulnerability affects core Framework and System components.

objects.name: CrowdStrike and Anthropic: Claude Cowork Security Integration
objects.description:
## Overview

CrowdStrike has partnered with Anthropic to provide runtime visibility and security for the Claude Cowork AI agent platform. Previously, code execution within Claude Cowork occurred inside an isolated virtual machine that served as a blind spot for host-based endpoint security sensors. By deploying a Falcon Linux sensor directly inside the Cowork VM, defenders can now monitor process, package, and network activity originating from the agent. This integration is currently in beta for macOS, with Windows support expected in late November 2026.

## Impact

The integration addresses the risk of AI agents inadvertently executing malicious code, such as compromised software packages, which could otherwise leverage mounted host folders to exfiltrate data without host-level visibility.

## Recommendation

* Inventory all workstations utilizing the Claude Cowork agent within the environment.
* Prepare for the beta deployment of the Falcon Linux sensor inside Claude Cowork virtual machines, beginning with macOS endpoints.
* Configure existing Falcon device management tools to support the forthcoming sensor deployment for the Windows platform, expected in late November 2026.

objects.name: Amlogic Android SDK: pppoe_wrapper root command injection (CVE-2026-119737)
objects.description:
## Overview

The pppoe_wrapper vendor daemon within the Amlogic Android SDK, utilized in devices such as the Nexbox A95X (Amlogic S905/S905X), is vulnerable to command injection. An attacker with local access can interact with a world-writable AF_UNIX datagram socket located at /dev/socket/pppoe_wrapper. By crafting a message starting with 'pppd pty' followed by shell metacharacters, the input is passed to system(3) and executed with root privileges via /system/bin/sh -c. This results in full system compromise. No patch information is currently provided.

## Impact

Successful exploitation results in full root privilege escalation on the affected Android device.

## Recommendation

Identify and audit devices running the Amlogic Android SDK for the presence of the world-writable /dev/socket/pppoe_wrapper socket. If the service is not required for production functionality, disable the pppoe_wrapper daemon or restrict access permissions to the socket file if the underlying operating system and hardware configuration permit.

objects.name: Azure AD: Federated identity credential addition to service principal
objects.description:
## Overview
Attackers can leverage the Entra ID (formerly Azure AD) workload identity federation feature to gain persistent access to service principals. By adding a new federated identity credential that points to an attacker-controlled OIDC issuer, a threat actor can authenticate as the service principal without requiring client secrets. This technique evades standard secrets monitoring and persists across credential rotations.

## Impact
Successful exploitation grants an attacker a persistent, secretless authentication path to the target service principal, potentially allowing for lateral movement, privilege escalation, or access to cloud resources protected by the service principal identity.

## Recommendation
- Baseline existing federated identity credentials across all service principals to identify legitimate OIDC configurations.
- Implement monitoring for the addition of new federated identity credentials, specifically focusing on unknown or unapproved OIDC issuers.
- Audit existing service principals for overly permissive subject claims in federated credentials.
- Use the hunt lead provided in the action plan to investigate current environment activity.

objects.name: Elastic Stack: LLM-based endpoint attack chain triage
objects.description:
## Overview
Elastic has introduced a higher-order detection rule for the Elastic Stack (9.4.0+) designed to reduce analyst alert fatigue. The rule uses ES|QL to aggregate disparate endpoint security alerts from a single host that occur within a 60-minute window. When at least three unique alert types are detected, the aggregated context (including process command lines, file paths, DNS queries, and registry modifications) is processed by an LLM via the Elastic Inference Service (EIS) to determine the likelihood of an active attack chain.

## Impact
The mechanism allows security operations teams to programmatically filter benign activity and prioritize hosts displaying correlated malicious behaviors, such as multi-stage intrusion attempts, without requiring manual cross-reference of individual alerts.

## Recommendation
- Deploy the rule 'LLM-Based Attack Chain Triage by Host' to existing Elastic Stack environments running version 9.4.0 or later.
- Ensure the Elastic Inference Service is configured with a supported LLM connector (e.g., Anthropic Claude Sonnet 4.6 or configured Azure/AWS/GCP alternatives) to power the triage logic.
- Baseline existing environment noise from legitimate testing frameworks, software package managers, and automated cloud instance bootstrapping to tune the triage results.
- Review high-confidence TP results (>0.9) as immediate candidates for host isolation or incident response escalation.

objects.name: ReadyMedia: Stack-based buffer overflow in DFF parsing (CVE-2026-29508)
objects.description:
## Overview

ReadyMedia (formerly MiniDLNA) versions 1.3.0 through 1.3.3 contain a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-29508). The issue arises during the parsing of DFF audio files when an oversized PROP chunk size is provided. This size is used to allocate a variable-length stack array without validation, leading to memory corruption when file data is read into the array.

## Impact

Successful exploitation may result in remote code execution (RCE) on systems without stack protections or a denial of service (DoS) on hardened systems. The vulnerability can be triggered automatically when the service parses a DFF file placed in a monitored directory using inotify.

## Recommendation

1. Inventory all instances of ReadyMedia/MiniDLNA to determine if versions 1.3.0 through 1.3.3 are in use.
2. Restrict file system write permissions for monitored directories to prevent unauthorized placement of malicious media files.
3. Monitor service logs for unexpected process termination or restarts, which may indicate crash-based exploitation attempts.
4. Apply security updates provided by the vendor once available; currently, upgrading to a version beyond 1.3.3 is required.

objects.name: Wavlink WN551X3-A: Remote OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-120345)
objects.description:
## Overview
CVE-2026-120345 is a remote OS command injection vulnerability in the DNS Resolution Handler (function sub_41a430 in /bin/ioos) of the Wavlink WN551X3-A router (specifically firmware version M51X3_V251020-WO-182e965). The vulnerability can be triggered by sending a maliciously crafted 'data' argument to the DNS resolution function. As the vulnerability is unauthenticated and a proof-of-concept exploit is publicly available, the risk to exposed devices is high.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands with the privileges of the DNS resolution service on the affected router. This can lead to full device compromise, persistence, and potential pivot points into internal networks.

## Recommendation
- Immediately inventory and restrict internet access to Wavlink WN551X3-A routers.
- Implement network segmentation to isolate these devices from critical infrastructure.
- Monitor logs for unusual traffic targeting router administrative or DNS management interfaces.
- Contact the vendor regarding availability of firmware updates for the affected model and version.

objects.name: SolarWinds Dameware: Authenticated Command Injection (CVE-2026-28336)
objects.description: SolarWinds Dameware was found to be affected by a command injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-28336) that could lead to the compromise of the remotely controlled host. Authentication is required to exploit this vulnerability. The CVSS v3.1 base score is 9.9.

objects.name: BITTER cyberespionage campaign utilizing PapRAT
objects.description: FortiGuard Labs has identified a cyberespionage campaign attributed to the threat actor BITTER. The campaign targets organizations in South Asia and utilizes three distinct attack chains to deliver the PapRAT remote access trojan.

objects.name: Dell OpenManage Enterprise: OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-94349)
objects.description: Dell OpenManage Enterprise versions prior to 4.8.0 contain an Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command vulnerability (CVE-2026-94349). A low-privileged attacker with adjacent network access could potentially exploit this to achieve command execution.

objects.name: AWS SDK for pandas: SQL identifier quoting vulnerability (CVE-2026-119301)
objects.description: CVE-2026-119301 describes a vulnerability in the Apache Iceberg write component of the AWS SDK for pandas (versions 3.5.2 through 3.17.0). Improper neutralization of quoting syntax in SQL identifier construction may allow an authenticated remote user with AWS Glue Data Catalog metadata modification permissions to read tables accessible by a more privileged principal and write to tables being updated by that principal via a crafted column name.

objects.name: Fastify: @fastify/reply-from path traversal (CVE-2026-117518)
objects.description:
## Overview

The @fastify/reply-from plugin (versions up to and including 12.8.0) fails to properly validate proxy paths containing backslash dot-segments. The WHATWG URL parser used by the plugin normalizes these backslashes to forward slashes, bypassing security guards intended to scope proxying to specific upstream prefixes. An attacker can exploit this to access restricted upstream API endpoints. The vulnerability is fixed in version 12.8.1.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated users to escape intended proxy boundaries, resulting in unauthorized access to unintended upstream resources. This is primarily a confidentiality impact with limited integrity impact.

## Recommendation

Update the @fastify/reply-from package to version 12.8.1 or later. There are no available workarounds.

objects.name: Google::Auth for Perl: SSRF and OAuth state validation vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-74759, CVE-2026-74760)
objects.description:
## Overview
Two vulnerabilities were disclosed in the Google::Auth Perl module. CVE-2026-74759 concerns an SSRF vulnerability occurring when the library processes unvalidated `credential_source` URLs while handling AWS external account credentials. CVE-2026-74760 involves an authentication bypass in the `gcloud-auth` login callback, which fails to verify OAuth state parameters, allowing an attacker to inject an authorization code from an unauthorized local process.

## Impact
CVE-2026-74759 may allow an attacker to force the application to make unauthorized requests to internal network resources. CVE-2026-74760 may lead to account takeover or unauthorized access to Google Cloud resources if an attacker successfully intercepts or injects a local authorization callback.

## Recommendation
* Update Google::Auth for Perl to a patched version that resolves these vulnerabilities.
* Audit applications using Google::Auth to identify usage of AWS external account credentials or local `gcloud-auth` login workflows.
* Restrict local network access for applications performing OAuth flows to prevent unauthorized local process interference.

objects.name: Adoption of Autonomous Agentic Frameworks for Offensive Operations
objects.description:
## Overview

Threat actors are increasingly weaponizing agentic, LLM-driven offensive frameworks - specifically ARTEX, Hexstrike, and CAIRN - to automate multiple stages of the attack lifecycle. These tools translate high-level tactical goals into machine commands, enabling rapid execution of reconnaissance, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. Unlike human operators, these frameworks exhibit distinct forensic characteristics, such as executing complex tasks in compressed bursts (2-25 seconds) and relying on iterative trial-and-error that generates high log volumes.

## Attack Chain

1. Initial Access: Adversaries utilize compromised credentials to gain entry.
2. Reconnaissance: Agentic frameworks profile target environments (e.g., Active Directory, cloud infrastructure/AWS security groups).
3. Exploitation: Frameworks target specific services, such as Linux web servers, using exposed application-specific APIs.
4. Execution/Persistence: Automated injection of malicious files; specifically, poisoning MySQL general logs via `SET GLOBAL general_log_file` to write webshells to public directories.
5. Lateral Movement: Autonomous exploration and pivot execution between services.
6. Exfiltration: Automated staging and preparation of stolen data.

## Impact

Automated attack frameworks enable adversaries to move from initial access to deep system access in significantly reduced timeframes, with observed incidents occurring in as little as 15 minutes. The high-volume, iterative nature of agentic activity increases the speed and scale of data theft and infrastructure exploitation.

## Recommendation

- Implement control-plane isolation to prevent automated tools from harvesting cloud service credentials.
- Enforce short-lived credentials and strict least-privilege policies to limit the scope of autonomous tool activity.
- Implement network segmentation to disrupt the lateral movement paths frequently probed by automated agents.
- Deploy behavioral analytics to detect rapid, burst-like execution patterns that deviate from human-paced administrative activity.

objects.name: Elastic Defend: Container Workload Protection Alert Aggregation
objects.description:
## Overview

The Elastic Defend for Containers integration provides visibility into container runtime threats, including potential container escapes, unauthorized access attempts, and orchestration anomalies. This detection rule serves as an aggregator for the `logs-cloud_defend.alerts-*` index, facilitating triage of alerts generated by the cloud defense module on Linux-based container hosts.

## Impact

Successful exploitation of containerized workloads can lead to unauthorized access to host systems, lateral movement within the container infrastructure, and disruption of containerized services.

## Recommendation

- Deploy the aggregate detection rule to your Elastic Security instance to capture alerts from the `cloud_defend` module.
- Baseline routine activities such as automated CI/CD deployments and scheduled maintenance tasks to create exceptions.
- Implement network segmentation and access controls to restrict exposure of the container orchestration plane.
- Configure alerts to trigger investigation workflows when events are received from `logs-cloud_defend.alerts-*`.

objects.name: Red Hat OpenShift: Bare metal provisioning controller information disclosure (CVE-2026-82976)
objects.description:
## Overview
A vulnerability in the image-customization-controller of OpenShift's bare metal provisioning stack allows unauthenticated network access to sensitive data. The controller hosts an HTTP file server on port 8084 that fails to implement authentication or authorization. The file system implementation permits a directory listing at the root path, which reveals image UUIDs. These images contain Ignition configuration files that include base64-encoded cluster pull secrets, potential IRONIC_RAMDISK_SSH_KEY values, proxy settings, and NetworkManager keyfiles. 

## Attack Chain
1. Attacker gains access to the provisioning network segment.
2. Attacker probes the OpenShift provisioning controller on TCP port 8084.
3. Attacker sends a GET request to the root path (/) to retrieve the browsable directory listing.
4. Attacker parses the response to enumerate all image file names (UUIDs).
5. Attacker downloads specific ISO or initramfs images using the enumerated UUIDs.
6. Attacker extracts the embedded Ignition configuration files from the downloaded images.
7. Attacker decodes the base64 cluster pull secrets and retrieves sensitive SSH keys and network configuration parameters.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows an adjacent attacker to gain unauthorized access to sensitive cluster credentials, including the cluster pull secret and SSH keys. This facilitates further compromise of the OpenShift environment or lateral movement within the provisioning network.

## Recommendation
- Restrict network access to port 8084 on the OpenShift image-customization-controller to trusted management or provisioning subnets using network policies or firewall rules.
- Audit existing Ignition configuration files for exposed secrets until a vendor patch is applied.
- Monitor logs for unauthorized HTTP requests to the provisioning controller endpoint, specifically directory listing attempts or bulk image downloads.

objects.name: Linux Kernel: Use-after-free in synthetic event reference counting (CVE-2026-99233)
objects.description:
## Overview
The Linux kernel tracing subsystem contains a vulnerability in `event_hist_trigger_parse()` and `hist_unreg_all()` where synthetic events are identified by basename rather than by `event_call` identity. 

Because `find_synth_event()` only compares the event basename, registering or removing a histogram on a non-synthetic trace event whose basename matches a synthetic event erroneously modifies the synthetic event's reference count. If a histogram is registered on the non-synthetic event and subsequently removed, the synthetic event's reference count may be decremented without a matching increment. This allows the synthetic event to be freed while an active histogram action still holds a pointer to it, resulting in a use-after-free condition.

objects.name: Nagios XI: OS command injection in MIB upload feature (CVE-2026-119742)
objects.description:
## Overview

Nagios XI versions prior to 2026R2 are susceptible to OS command injection via the MIB upload functionality. The vulnerability exists within the install_mib() function in mibs.php, which fails to adequately sanitize uploaded filenames. Specifically, the character-substitution filter omits semicolons, pipes, and non-space IFS (Internal Field Separator) whitespace characters before passing the filename to a grep command executed via the system exec() function. An authenticated administrator can bypass this filter by utilizing tab characters within a multipart POST request to mibs.php, leading to command execution under the context of the web server user.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows an authenticated administrator to execute arbitrary OS commands as the web server user, potentially leading to full system compromise of the Nagios XI server.

## Recommendation

- Upgrade Nagios XI to version 2026R2 or later immediately to patch the vulnerable install_mib() function.
- Review administrative account activity for unauthorized access or suspicious changes to MIB configurations.
- Restrict access to the MIB upload feature to only highly trusted administrative users until the patch is applied.

objects.name: Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced: Missing authentication remote code execution (CVE-2026-58115)
objects.description:
## Overview

Siemens SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed are vulnerable to a missing authentication flaw (CVE-2026-58115) within the Node-RED HTTP interface. This vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to create malicious flows, execute arbitrary code, and establish persistent backdoors with maximum privileges. The issue was remediated in version 4.3.4.1. Active exploitation attempts have been observed, involving the deployment of secondary botnet binaries and shell scripts.

## Attack Chain

1. Attacker sends a crafted, unauthenticated HTTP request to the Node-RED interface of the targeted SIMATIC IoT2050 device.
2. The malicious request deploys a Node-RED flow to the target.
3. The flow is automatically triggered upon deployment.
4. The flow executes a shell command wrapper using the internal 'exec' node.
5. The shell wrapper utilizes 'wget' or 'curl' to retrieve a secondary payload from an attacker-controlled server (e.g., 85.215.73.250).
6. The retrieved binary or script is saved to a directory such as '/dev/shm/' or '/tmp/'.
7. The payload is executed to establish the botnet presence or expose an arbitrary command-execution endpoint (e.g., /cmd).

## Recommendation

- Upgrade SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced firmware to version 4.3.4.1 or later immediately.
- If upgrading is not possible, uninstall Node-RED from the device.
- If Node-RED is required, harden the interface by enabling HTTPS and enforcing credential-based authentication for the editor, Admin API, HTTP nodes, and Dashboard.
- Block communication to identified malicious IPs (85.215.73.250 and 45.194.90.57) at the network perimeter.
- Audit Node-RED instances for unexpected HTTP endpoints or active "exec" nodes in configured flows.

objects.name: Elo: Ruby backend arbitrary code execution (CVE-2026-44266)
objects.description: Elo, a functional expression language, contains a vulnerability in its Ruby backend (src/compilers/ruby.ts). Attacker-controlled text is embedded into Ruby double-quoted strings without escaping '#', allowing Ruby interpolation to become executable. A failing labelled subtype constraint or an ordinary string literal can lead to Ruby code and shell command execution via backticks. Affected entry points include the /try playground (Ruby target), bin/eloc -t ruby -x, and defaultFormats.elo.parse() followed by Ruby emission. This issue is fixed in version 1.0.1.

objects.name: VStarcam O-KAM SuperIPCam: Use-after-free vulnerability (CVE-2026-120337)
objects.description: CVE-2026-120337 is a use-after-free vulnerability in VStarcam O-KAM SuperIPCam version 1.3.3.32. The vulnerability affects the function FUN_005a2d44 of SuperIPCam.exe within the P2P Session Teardown component. The vulnerability can be initiated remotely. Public exploit code has been disclosed. The vendor was contacted but did not respond.

objects.name: Linux Local Group Enumeration via Standard Utilities
objects.description:
## Overview

Adversaries often perform local group enumeration to identify target accounts for privilege escalation or lateral movement. Threat actors use common Linux system utilities, such as 'getent', 'groups', and various file readers, to query '/etc/group' or '/etc/gshadow' files to gain visibility into system account permissions and administrative group membership.

## Impact

The impact of group enumeration is primarily reconnaissance. Successful discovery allows an attacker to identify high-privilege users or security groups, facilitating subsequent phases of an attack such as credential harvesting or privilege escalation.

## Recommendation

Deploy the provided Sigma detection rule to monitor process executions involving sensitive group files or enumeration tools. Because these utilities are heavily used for legitimate system administration, focus analysis on deviations from established administrative baselines or account behavior.

objects.name: Zohocorp ManageEngine Eventlog Analyzer and Log360: Authenticated remote code execution (CVE-2026-8923)
objects.description:
## Overview
Zohocorp ManageEngine Eventlog Analyzer and ManageEngine Log360 versions before 13062 are vulnerable to authenticated remote code execution (RCE) via the Log Forwarding configuration option. An attacker with valid credentials can leverage this feature to execute arbitrary code on the underlying host system.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows an authenticated user to achieve remote code execution on the server hosting the ManageEngine application, potentially leading to full system compromise.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade ManageEngine Eventlog Analyzer and ManageEngine Log360 to version 13062 or later immediately.
- Audit existing ManageEngine administrative accounts and restrict access to the Log Forwarding configuration interface to verified administrators only.
- Review historical logs for any unusual modifications to log forwarding settings or suspicious process execution spawning from the ManageEngine service account.

objects.name: HotGo: Authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-120447)
objects.description:
## Overview

HotGo through version 2.15.1 is affected by an authentication bypass vulnerability. An attacker can manipulate the SMS login process by supplying a user-defined value in the Code field during a request to the /admin/sms/send endpoint. By knowing a target user's mobile number, an attacker can set a known verification code and subsequently authenticate through the /admin/site/mobileLogin endpoint to compromise the account.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated attackers to gain unauthorized access to any user account, including those with administrative privileges, resulting in full account takeover.

## Recommendation

Identify all HotGo deployments within the environment. As of this report, no specific patch version is listed, but users should monitor the vendor for a security update to address CVE-2026-120447 and apply it immediately upon release.

objects.name: IBM App Connect Enterprise: Denial of Service vulnerability
objects.description:
## Overview

IBM App Connect Enterprise contains a vulnerability that allows a remote, unauthenticated attacker to cause a Denial of Service (DoS) condition. Details regarding the specific vulnerable components or the nature of the exploit have not been publicly disclosed. Users should monitor official IBM security bulletins for remediation guidance and patch availability.

## Impact

The vulnerability allows an unauthenticated attacker to remotely disrupt the availability of the IBM App Connect Enterprise service.

## Recommendation

- Inventory all internet-facing and internal instances of IBM App Connect Enterprise.
- Monitor the official IBM support portal for forthcoming security patches addressing this DoS vulnerability.
- Restrict network access to management interfaces and sensitive service ports to authorized networks only.

objects.name: PostgreSQL: psqlODBC memory corruption vulnerability (CVE-2026-120064)
objects.description:
Several psqlODBC entry points use application-supplied column numbers or row indexes as array indexes without validation. 
- `SQLBindCol` with a column number above 32767 can cause the binding count to wrap negative, leading to out-of-bounds array access.
- Negative `SQL_DESC_COUNT` on an application row descriptor results in unbinding columns at negative indexes.
- `SQLColAttribute` with a large column number can use a negative index.
- `SQLSetPos(SQL_ADD)` fails to validate the row number against the rowset size.
An application that forwards untrusted column or row numbers exposes its process to out-of-bounds reads and writes. Versions before psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.

objects.name: Traefik: Multiple security control bypass vulnerabilities
objects.description:
## Overview
The German Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) has released an advisory regarding multiple vulnerabilities in Traefik that allow for the bypass of security mechanisms. No specific CVE IDs or technical exploit details have been disclosed in this initial advisory. Organizations using Traefik are advised to monitor for official vendor patches and technical updates from Traefik Labs.

## Recommendation
- Inventory all internet-facing and internal Traefik proxy deployments.
- Monitor the Traefik Labs security advisory portal for pending release information and patch availability.
- Implement strict ingress filtering and review access logs for anomalous traffic patterns directed at the proxy infrastructure.

objects.name: HPE Networking Fabric Composer: Authenticated Sensitive Information Disclosure (CVE-2026-95734)
objects.description: CVE-2026-95734 is a sensitive information disclosure vulnerability in the HPE Networking Fabric Composer API. The vulnerability allows an authenticated low-privileged user to access sensitive information, including stored credentials, beyond their authorized privilege level. A proof-of-concept exploit has been published on Sploitus.

objects.name: Linksys E8450: Stack-based buffer overflow in portal.cgi (CVE-2026-120283)
objects.description: A vulnerability was identified in Linksys E8450 firmware version 1.2.00.360516. The issue involves the `strcpy` function in the file `/www/cgi-bin/portal.cgi`. Manipulation of the `hidden_timezone` argument leads to a stack-based buffer overflow. The attack can be executed remotely. The vendor was contacted regarding this disclosure but did not respond.

objects.name: Modem: Out-of-bounds write vulnerability (CVE-2026-20499)
objects.description:
## Overview

CVE-2026-20499 is a memory corruption vulnerability in Modem firmware identified by the lack of bounds checking. The vulnerability allows for remote privilege escalation when a User Equipment (UE) device connects to a rogue base station controlled by an attacker. The vulnerability (MSV-8247) is addressed by Patch ID MOLY01857954.

## Impact

An attacker can achieve remote privilege escalation on a target device without user interaction or prior elevated execution privileges by forcing the device to connect to a malicious base station.

## Recommendation

* Verify the current firmware version of all cellular-connected UEs in the environment.
* Apply patch MOLY01857954 (Issue MSV-8247) to all affected Modem hardware.
* Implement cellular network monitoring to identify anomalies in base station parameters or signal strength characteristics that may indicate rogue base station activity.

objects.name: Babelfish for PostgreSQL: Improper access control vulnerability (CVE-2026-119922)
objects.description: Babelfish for PostgreSQL versions 1.2-1.5, 2.1-2.15, 3.1-3.12, 4.0-4.8, and 5.1-5.4 contain an improper access control vulnerability (CVE-2026-119922) that may allow remote authenticated users to elevate their privileges. The CVSS v3.1 base score for this vulnerability is 8.8. To remediate this issue, it is recommended to upgrade to Babelfish for PostgreSQL extension versions 4.10, 5.6, 6.1 or later.

objects.name: Control Web Panel: OS command injection in protected_directory (CVE-2026-77876)
objects.description: Control Web Panel (CWP) before webpanel_version 1.16 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in the protected_directory user panel module. The flaw allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands by submitting unescaped input through the 'file' POST parameter in the 'acc=deletedp' action. This occurs because the application passes attacker-controlled input directly into a shell_exec call, allowing code execution in the user panel context.

objects.name: LLMJacking: Cybercriminal Resale of Stolen Cloud LLM Access
objects.description:
## Overview
Threat actors are increasingly monetizing compromised cloud infrastructure through a practice termed LLMJacking. Attackers gain initial access to organizations, specifically targeting LLM endpoints and associated API keys. Once access is established, the stolen resources are aggregated and resold through underground "LLM Mixer" services. This model allows attackers to profit by routing customer requests through the victim’s environment, often resulting in significant, rapid financial losses for the victim due to cloud resource consumption billing.

## Attack Chain
1. Initial Access: Attackers obtain cloud identity tokens, service account keys, or GitHub Personal Access Tokens (PATs) via phishing, session hijacking, or exploitation of web vulnerabilities in containerized environments.
2. Credential Validation: Attackers perform minimal API requests, often sending a single output token, to verify the validity of stolen credentials while remaining under detection thresholds.
3. Persistence Establishment: Attackers use compromised federation tokens to programmatically generate new, long-lived access keys, bypassing existing MFA controls.
4. Infrastructure Integration: Compromised credentials are integrated into underground "LLM Mixer" services, which act as middlemen to resell enterprise LLM capacity.
5. Resource Abuse: The mixer service routes external customer requests through the victim’s cloud environment, causing rapid spikes in computing resource consumption.
6. Monetization: The threat actor collects subscription fees from the reseller network while the victim organization absorbs the high costs of the unauthorized LLM inference requests.

## Impact
Observed impacts include rapid spikes in cloud resource consumption. Incidents have resulted in fraudulent charges exceeding $100,000 USD in a single day, with cumulative costs for some organizations reaching $1 million USD before access was revoked.

## Recommendation
- Implement centralized secrets management to rotate and restrict service account keys and API credentials.
- Enforce the principle of least privilege for all cloud service accounts and API access tokens.
- Deploy automated secret scanning tools across internal code repositories (e.g., GitHub, GitLab) to prevent accidental exposure of tokens.
- Establish automated billing and resource consumption alerts to identify unauthorized usage spikes in real-time.
- Implement rate limiting and network allow-listing for all public-facing LLM endpoints.

objects.name: Elastic Defend: Higher-Order Detection for Multi-Rule Host Compromise
objects.description:
## Overview

This detection rule leverages ES|QL INLINE STATS to identify hosts that trigger two or more distinct Elastic Defend behavior alerts within a 60-minute window, where each alert is globally rare (triggered on only one host). The rule is designed to prioritize investigation on hosts exhibiting multiple anomalous behaviors, which often indicate successful compromise or post-exploitation activity. It requires Elastic Stack version 9.4.0 or higher.

## Recommendation

- Deploy the 'Multiple Rare Elastic Defend Behavior Rules by Host' rule in environments using Elastic Defend.
- Tune the rule by adding exceptions for known-good administrative scripts or development environments that frequently trigger multiple rare behavioral alerts.
- Investigate flagged hosts by reviewing the specific behavior rule names, parent process command lines, and associated user accounts surfaced by the rule's output fields.
- Prioritize triage for hosts where the flagged activity includes unusual process command lines or indicators of lateral movement.

objects.name: DoraCMS: Mass assignment in user API key management (CVE-2026-120448)
objects.description:
## Overview
DoraCMS through version 3.1.0 contains a mass assignment vulnerability in the PUT /api/v1/user/api-keys/:id endpoint. An authenticated, low-privileged user can manipulate the 'userId' field in a PUT request to associate their own API key with a victim's account. This allows the attacker to impersonate the victim, enabling unauthorized modifications to profiles, content publication, and content deletion.

## Impact
Successful exploitation grants an attacker the privileges of a targeted user, which may include administrative rights depending on the victim's account level. This allows for unauthorized profile changes, as well as the deletion or modification of content within the DoraCMS instance.

## Recommendation
- Update DoraCMS to the latest available version containing the patch for CVE-2026-120448.
- Review web server access logs for anomalous PUT requests directed at the /api/v1/user/api-keys/ endpoint.
- Audit existing API key ownership and monitor for unexpected changes in key-to-user mappings.

objects.name: Barracuda Networks: Pre-authentication Authorization Bypass and Command Injection
objects.description:
## Overview

Barracuda Networks has disclosed multiple security vulnerabilities affecting a wide range of its appliance products. The vulnerabilities are identified as pre-authentication authorization bypass and command injection. Unauthenticated remote attackers may be able to bypass security controls or execute arbitrary system commands on the affected devices. 

## Recommendation

Prioritize patching of all internet-facing Barracuda appliances to the following minimum versions:

* Barracuda Email Security Gateway (ESG): Update to 9.4.0.030 or later.
* Barracuda Load Balancer ADC: Update to 6.4.0 or later.
* Barracuda Web Application Firewall (WAF): Update to 11.0.1 or later.
* Barracuda Web Security Gateway (WSG): Update to 16.1.100.100 or later.
* Barracuda Message Archiver (BMA): Update to 5.5.4.0 or later.
* Barracuda WAF Control Center (WCC): Update to 2.2.1 or later.

Administrators should monitor appliance audit logs for unusual management interface access attempts or unexpected process execution spawned by web service accounts.

objects.name: Krill: Authentication bypass in RPKI provisioning (CVE-2026-109142)
objects.description: CVE-2026-109142 is an authentication bypass vulnerability in Krill. When a CA's parent lives on the same Krill server, the system fails to verify that the child identity (child_handle) belongs to the CA making the request. Instead, it runs the RFC 6492 provisioning exchange in-process and trusts the child identity provided by the caller in the parent contact.

objects.name: Microsoft Entra ID: Managed Device Client Sign-In to Graph Enumeration
objects.description:
## Overview
This threat brief describes a detection pattern for unauthorized Microsoft Graph API usage. It correlates non-interactive Microsoft Entra ID sign-ins (asserting managed, Azure AD joined device context and an Edge user agent) with subsequent activity where the exact access token is used by a scripted client to query at least three distinct directory-enumeration paths in Microsoft Graph. This approach utilizes the unique token identifier to correlate activity, rather than relying on session identifiers.

objects.name: Linux Kernel: io_uring waitid reference counter wrap (CVE-2026-99227)
objects.description: The Linux kernel io_uring/waitid implementation packs cancellation state into bit 31 of a reference counter, using the remaining bits as a 31-bit reference counter. Repeated failed cancellation attempts incorrectly increment the reference counter, which can lead to a wrap-around to zero. This state allows a subsequent cancellation attempt to claim ownership and complete the request a second time.

objects.name: FluentCart: Arbitrary file deletion (CVE-2026-120577)
objects.description:
## Overview
The FluentCart plugin for WordPress (versions 1.6.2 and earlier) is susceptible to an arbitrary file deletion vulnerability. This flaw stems from improper file path validation within the plugin's `deleteFile` function. Authenticated users with custom-level access or higher can leverage this vulnerability to delete critical files on the web server, such as `wp-config.php`, which can result in application compromise or remote code execution.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows for the deletion of arbitrary files on the hosting server. Deleting critical application configuration files, such as `wp-config.php`, may force the application into an installation state or facilitate further exploitation leading to remote code execution.

## Recommendation
- Update the FluentCart plugin to the latest available version (beyond 1.6.2) to remediate the path validation flaw.
- Review WordPress user role assignments to ensure that users with custom-level access and above are limited to trusted individuals.
- Audit web server file access logs for requests targeting the `deleteFile` function logic, typically associated with administrative or plugin-specific API endpoints.

objects.name: OpenAirInterface Core Network: Stack-based buffer overflow in UDM (CVE-2026-106808)
objects.description: A stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability exists in OpenAirInterface (OAI) Core Network v2.2.1 within the Nudm_UEAU Generate Authentication Data endpoint. The UDM fails to validate the size of `resynchronizationInfo.rand` and `auts` values when passed to `conv::hex_str_to_uint8()`. An unauthenticated attacker with access to the SBI interface and a valid SUPI can provide an oversized value to overwrite adjacent stack memory and the stack canary, causing the UDM process to terminate.

objects.name: JetBrains Toolbox App and IntelliJ IDEA: Security bypass vulnerability
objects.description:
## Overview

The BSI has released an advisory regarding a security vulnerability in JetBrains Toolbox App and IntelliJ IDEA. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can exploit this flaw to bypass security controls within the affected applications. No specific CVE identifier or exploitation details have been disclosed at this time. 

## Recommendation

- Inventory all installations of JetBrains Toolbox App and IntelliJ IDEA across the organization.
- Monitor vendor advisory channels for patch availability and specific update instructions from JetBrains.
- Prioritize applying security updates immediately upon release by the vendor to address this bypass vulnerability.

objects.name: SureCart: Unauthenticated account takeover vulnerability (CVE-2026-120574)
objects.description: The SureCart plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to unauthenticated account takeover in all versions up to, and including, 4.9.5. The passwordless one-time-code login REST route (VerificationCodeController::verify()) resolves an attacker-supplied login to any WordPress user, verifies a 6-digit code, and calls wp_set_auth_cookie() for that user. This path lacks per-account attempt counters, persistent email/IP lockout, or rate limits. An unauthenticated attacker can trigger a code for any user via a companion endpoint and brute-force the 6-digit code to obtain an authenticated session as that user, resulting in a full administrator account takeover.

objects.name: Control Web Panel: Authentication bypass via execution after redirect (CVE-2026-73696)
objects.description:
## Overview

Control Web Panel (CWP) versions before 1.12 are vulnerable to an execution after redirect flaw within the user panel authentication process. The unauthenticatedFlow() function in CWPUserIndex initiates a redirect to the login page via toLoginWithIntendedUri() but fails to call exit(), which allows the PHP script execution to proceed. This flaw permits an attacker with a valid hosting username to reach module code paths that should be restricted, potentially leading to unauthorized access and privilege escalation.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated users with a valid hosting account to bypass security controls and interact with internal user-panel modules, which can facilitate a chain of exploitation leading to root-level compromise of the server.

## Recommendation

Update all Control Web Panel instances to version 1.12 or later immediately to address the vulnerable authentication logic.

objects.name: FreeRDP: Denial of Service in WinPR via malformed clipboard images (CVE-2026-121386)
objects.description:
## Overview

FreeRDP versions before 3.32.2 contain a denial of service vulnerability located in the WinPR library's `winpr_read_png_from_buffer()` and `winpr_convert_from_jpeg()` functions. The vulnerability stems from insufficient error handling when interacting with the `libpng` and `libjpeg` libraries. An attacker acting as a malicious RDP server or performing a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attack can trigger this flaw by providing a malformed PNG or a truncated JPEG payload via the RDP clipboard channel. Successful exploitation causes the FreeRDP client process to abort or terminate unexpectedly.

## Impact

The vulnerability allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to cause a denial of service by crashing the client application. No code execution is documented as part of this vulnerability.

## Recommendation

Update all instances of the FreeRDP client to version 3.32.2 or later immediately to incorporate the required error handling for image processing functions.

objects.name: Azure Resource Manager: Unauthorized resource group deletion detection
objects.description:
## Overview
Azure Resource Group deletion is a permanent operation that removes all contained resources. Attackers may leverage this to perform data destruction, impair recovery by removing snapshots or backups, or cause operational disruption. This detection uses an ES|QL first-seen approach to alert on resource group deletions performed by principals that have not executed this action in the preceding 7 days, helping to filter routine infrastructure-as-code or CI/CD activity while flagging anomalous identity behavior.

## Impact
Deletion of a resource group is irreversible and removes all resources within it. Observed impact can range from authorized environment teardown by automated pipelines to unauthorized destruction of production infrastructure or defensive evasion by clearing logs and supporting resources.

## Recommendation
- Deploy the ES|QL detection logic provided by Elastic to flag first-time resource group deletions.
- Establish a baseline of known CI/CD, IaC, and platform service principals and investigate any alerts triggered by identities outside this scope.
- Implement Azure Policy or management locks on critical production resource groups to prevent accidental or unauthorized deletion.
- Require privileged delete operations to proceed via Privileged Identity Management (PIM) or approved change-control pipelines.

objects.name: Dockhand: Path traversal vulnerability (CVE-2026-121448)
objects.description:
## Overview
Dockhand versions prior to 1.0.54 contain a path traversal vulnerability. Authenticated users can exploit this by providing double-encoded input (e.g., %252e%252e) within the stack name parameter of the /api/stacks/[name]/env/raw endpoint. This allows unauthorized access to sensitive .env files located outside the intended stack root directory.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows authenticated attackers to disclose cross-environment secrets, overwrite critical configuration files, or poison deployment variables by deleting or modifying .env files.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade Dockhand to version 1.0.54 or later immediately.
- Audit logs for the /api/stacks/ endpoint to identify attempts containing encoded dot-dot sequences.
- Rotate secrets contained within any .env files that may have been accessible during the period of exposure.

objects.name: BuddyBoss App: Arbitrary File Upload in send_feedback function (CVE-2026-76124)
objects.description: The BuddyBoss App plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Upload in all versions up to and including 3.2.1 via the send_feedback function. The vulnerability arises from insufficient file type validation that relies on the client-supplied Content-Type header. Authenticated users with subscriber-level access and above can upload executable files. While files are intended to be deleted after transmission, a race condition during SMTP execution or a failure of the wp_mail() function can allow files to persist on the server.

objects.name: PyMuPDF: Stack-based buffer overflow in JM_set_annot_callout_line (CVE-2026-120752)
objects.description:
## Overview

PyMuPDF versions before 2.0 contain a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the function JM_set_annot_callout_line. The function fails to validate the number of callout points supplied by the caller, copying them into a fixed three-element stack array. An attacker controlling the callout argument passed to the Page.add_freetext_annot method can provide four or more points to overwrite the stack frame. Successful exploitation may result in a crash of the host process or arbitrary code execution.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows for memory corruption within the application process, leading to denial of service via process crash or potential arbitrary code execution under the context of the user or service running the PyMuPDF library.

## Recommendation

Upgrade all instances of PyMuPDF to version 2.0 or later immediately to incorporate the bounds checking fix for the JM_set_annot_callout_line function. Perform an inventory of internal applications and third-party software that utilize the PyMuPDF library to identify instances requiring updates.

objects.name: AzuraCast: Remote code execution via station timezone injection (CVE-2026-121428)
objects.description: AzuraCast through 0.23.8 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated station managers to inject Supervisor configuration through the station timezone field. Attackers can submit a timezone containing newlines to the profile edit API, defining a new Supervisor program that executes OS commands as root when configuration regenerates.

objects.name: traQ: Stored cross-site scripting via file upload (CVE-2026-63197)
objects.description:
## Overview
traQ messenger application versions prior to 3.28.3 contain a vulnerability when configured with `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE=local`. The `/files/{fileId}` retrieval endpoint returns user-uploaded SVG or HTML content without adequate security headers or sanitization, causing browsers to render the files directly. An attacker with file-upload privileges can upload malicious files containing JavaScript to trigger XSS in the context of other users who view the file.

## Impact
Successful exploitation allows an attacker to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser session. This can lead to session hijacking, unauthorized actions performed on behalf of the user, or theft of sensitive information stored within the traQ application session.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade traQ to version 3.28.3 or later immediately.
- For instances where immediate patching is not possible, disable local file storage by modifying the `TRAQ_STORAGE_TYPE` configuration if feasible, or implement strict Content Security Policy (CSP) headers on the web server hosting the traQ application to restrict the execution of inline scripts and unauthorized sources.
- Audit logs for the `/files/{fileId}` endpoint to identify unusual access patterns or requests for files with SVG/HTML extensions from suspicious user agents.

objects.name: Grafana Mimir and Enterprise Metrics: Alertmanager arbitrary file read (CVE-2026-81938)
objects.description: Grafana Mimir's Alertmanager does not properly validate tenant-supplied receiver configurations that reference local files. Specifically, the `http_headers.<name>.files` and `basic_auth.username_file` settings allow a tenant to point to any file readable by the Alertmanager process. When a notification is sent, Alertmanager reads the file and includes its contents in a header of the outgoing request. By directing the receiver to an attacker-controlled server, the tenant can exfiltrate sensitive files, such as credentials and configuration, from the host.

objects.name: SD-JWT JS: Disclosure omission and validation bypass (CVE-2026-62374)
objects.description:
The `@sd-jwt/decode` and `@sd-jwt/core` libraries (version 0.19.0) contain a validation flaw in the disclosure processing layer that deviates from RFC 9901 requirements. The libraries perform a lossy decoding process that silently drops tampered or non-decodable disclosures instead of rejecting the presentation.

When a disclosure is tampered with (e.g., via byte manipulation or invalid UTF-8 sequences), the library fails to identify the mismatch against the Issuer-signed `_sd` array. Consequently, the library returns a successful verification result containing a reduced claim set. This behavior acts as an omission primitive, potentially allowing holders or on-path attackers to bypass authorization logic that assumes the presence of specific credentials.

The issue specifically violates:
- RFC 9901 §7.1 step 5: Mandatory rejection if any disclosure is not referenced by digest in the signed JWT.
- RFC 9901 §7.1 step 3 / §4.2.1: Mandatory rejection of non-base64url-JSON disclosures.

objects.name: Petpooja Munshi: Payment bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-119731)
objects.description: Munshi (by Petpooja) before 2026-06-30 contained a payment bypass vulnerability in its subscription payment webhook at POST /api/payment/order/webhook. The endpoint lacks webhook authentication, cryptographic signature verification, source validation, and independent server-side confirmation with the payment provider. A remote, unauthenticated attacker can submit a forged payment-success notification referencing an order obtained from the payment-status redirect URL, causing the backend to mark the subscription as paid/active and granting paid access without an actual successful payment.

objects.name: LogChimp: Authorization bypass in post modification (CVE-2026-121560)
objects.description: LogChimp before version 0.9.3 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability. Authenticated post authors can modify any other post by supplying mismatched postId and id body parameters. This allows an attacker to overwrite the title, slug, content, boardId, and roadmap_id of a victim's post by using an enumerated victim post UUID.

objects.name: AzuraCast: Configuration injection and privilege escalation (CVE-2026-121427)
objects.description:
## Overview
AzuraCast versions 0.23.8 and earlier are vulnerable to a configuration injection attack via the /station/{id}/profile/edit endpoint. The application fails to properly validate permissions or sanitize input for the frontend_config.custom_config field. Authenticated users with the Manage station profile permission can inject arbitrary directives into the Shoutcast sc_serv.conf file, enabling them to override critical security settings such as adminpassword and portbase.

## Impact
An attacker can hijack the Shoutcast frontend service by overriding authentication credentials and service configuration parameters, leading to a complete compromise of the station broadcasting service.

## Recommendation
- Upgrade AzuraCast to a version later than 0.23.8 once a patch is available.
- Review existing permissions for all users assigned the Manage station profile role to identify unauthorized configuration changes.
- Monitor logs for HTTP PUT requests to /station/*/profile/edit that include unusual JSON structures in the custom_config field.

objects.name: Elastic: Improper certificate validation in OS certificate bundles (CVE-2026-115714)
objects.description: CVE-2026-115714 identifies an improper certificate validation vulnerability (CWE-295) affecting the operating system certificate bundle used by several Elastic products, including APM Server, various Beats (Auditbeat, Filebeat, Heartbeat, Metricbeat, Packetbeat), Elastic Agent (including Fleet Server and Cloudbeat), Logstash, Elastic connectors, Universal Profiling, and Elastic Maps Server. The bundle includes eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities whose private keys are compromised. This allows an attacker in a network position between the product and a remote party to intercept or modify TLS-protected traffic by presenting a certificate issued by these compromised keys.

objects.name: Binance: Multi-stage social engineering and supply chain campaign
objects.description:
## Overview

Binance disclosed a multi-stage campaign that led to the theft of $6.43 billion from their exchange infrastructure. The campaign utilized a mix of supply chain compromise via trojanized software and recruitment-themed social engineering to compromise multiple engineers. Attackers gained access to internal systems, including an AI tool and container deployment infrastructure, ultimately reaching the internal wallet signing service to initiate unauthorized transactions.

## Attack Chain

1. Initial Compromise: An engineer downloaded a trojanized Homebrew installer after searching for an AI tool.
2. Credential Exposure: The initial compromise exposed the engineer's role and internal wallet infrastructure metadata.
3. Secondary Social Engineering: A different engineer was contacted via a job-hunting platform by an actor masquerading as a Project Director.
4. Malware Execution: The target engineer was directed to download a malicious "assignment" repository, which executed obfuscated malware on their workstation.
5. Internal Tool Abuse: Attackers used the compromised workstation to hijack an internal AI tool.
6. Credential Harvesting: Stolen credentials and a container deployment token were used to move laterally to a third engineer's workstation.
7. Unauthorized Transaction: The attacker deployed a malicious container to reach the internal wallet signing service and initiate unauthorized transactions.

## Impact

The breach resulted in the confirmed theft of $6.43 billion in assets from the exchange. Binance reported that they have since reconstructed the affected wallet system, rebuilt internal tools, and decommissioned all compromised credentials.

## Recommendation

- Implement strict endpoint controls on developer workstations, specifically restricting the installation of packages from unverified or public repositories (e.g., Homebrew).
- Enforce hardware-based multi-factor authentication for all internal AI tools and sensitive infrastructure access tokens.
- Implement behavioral anomaly detection for internal CI/CD and container deployment pipelines.
- Audit and rotate all high-privilege credentials and session tokens upon any suspicion of endpoint compromise.
- Establish a formal verification process for recruitment-related file downloads or interview-related technical assessments.

objects.name: madong-admin-saas: Missing authentication in tenant management API (CVE-2026-120446)
objects.description:
## Overview

CVE-2026-120446 is a critical authentication bypass vulnerability in the 'madong-admin-saas' platform. The flaw originates from a middleware configuration error where the 'platformapi' key fails to validate against the 'platform' application, effectively disabling authentication for specific API endpoints. Unauthenticated attackers can access, modify, or delete tenant accounts and subscription plans by interacting directly with the exposed API.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated remote attackers to list, create, modify, disable, or delete tenants, and modify subscription plans via the platform tenant management API.

## Recommendation

1. Inventory all instances of 'madong-admin-saas' running version 5.1.4 or earlier.
2. Prioritize upgrading to the latest patched version of the software.
3. If immediate patching is not possible, apply network access control lists (ACLs) to restrict access to the /platformapi/ endpoints to known-trusted management IP ranges.
4. Implement logging for all requests to the /platformapi/tenant/account, bind-plan, and sync-data endpoints to identify unauthorized access attempts.

objects.name: GoFound: Path traversal arbitrary directory deletion (CVE-2026-120444)
objects.description:
## Overview

GoFound through version 1.4.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the database parameter. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this via crafted GET requests to the /api/db/create and /api/db/drop endpoints. By injecting dot-dot-slash (../) sequences into the parameter, the application performs an os.RemoveAll operation on directories outside the intended data directory, leading to arbitrary directory deletion.

## Impact

Successful exploitation allows unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary directories on the server hosting the GoFound application, potentially resulting in system instability, data loss, or denial of service depending on the target path.

## Recommendation

- Upgrade GoFound to a version beyond 1.4.1 once a security update is released by the maintainers.
- Audit access logs for requests to /api/db/create and /api/db/drop containing path traversal characters.
- Restrict network access to the GoFound API management endpoints to authorized management IP addresses only.

objects.name: Linux Kernel: Bluetooth L2CAP Race Condition (CVE-2026-99239)
objects.description: A vulnerability exists in the Linux kernel Bluetooth stack where a TOCTOU race condition allows an l2cap_chan to be linked to an l2cap_conn multiple times. This violates an invariant assumed by cleanup functions such as l2cap_chan_del. The vulnerability occurs because l2cap_sock_connect does not check sk->sk_state, potentially triggering a second __l2cap_chan_add call. The fix includes an invariant check in __l2cap_chan_add and introduces locking in l2cap_sock_bind to protect the channel state.

objects.name: MongoDB C Driver: Out-of-bounds heap memory disclosure (CVE-2026-120956)
objects.description:
## Overview
The MongoDB C Driver lacks validation for the type and format of 'namespace' fields returned by a MongoDB server. An unauthenticated attacker-controlled MongoDB endpoint can exploit this by returning a malformed namespace value in a query response. This results in either a process termination (denial of service) or an out-of-bounds memory read, leading to the leakage of the client application's uninitialized heap memory via subsequent commands. The impact is isolated to the client application process embedding the vulnerable driver.

## Impact
Confirmed impacts include process termination (Denial of Service) and the potential exposure of sensitive data stored in uninitialized heap memory to a malicious server endpoint.

## Recommendation
- Inventory all internal applications and services that utilize the MongoDB C Driver.
- Prioritize updates to the driver as soon as a patch is released by MongoDB to address the lack of input validation.
- Monitor client applications for unexpected crashes or error patterns that correlate with MongoDB connectivity.

objects.name: XWiki: Remote information disclosure vulnerability
objects.description:
## Overview

The BSI has reported an information disclosure vulnerability in XWiki that can be exploited by an unauthenticated, remote attacker. No further technical details, specific CVE identifiers, or impacted versions have been disclosed in the initial advisory.

## Recommendation

- Monitor vendor security bulletins for updates regarding affected versions and patches.
- Review XWiki deployment logs for unusual access patterns or repeated unauthorized requests to sensitive internal endpoints.
- Apply security patches as soon as they are made available by the vendor.

objects.name: Netpbm: Heap-based buffer overflow in sgitopnm (CVE-2026-120431)
objects.description:
## Overview
Netpbm versions before 10.86.51, 11.x before 11.02.29, and 11.03 before 11.15.07 are affected by a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the `sgitopnm` utility. The flaw exists within the `readChannels()` function and is triggered when processing RLE-compressed SGI images containing an oversized offset table. Successful exploitation can result in application crashes or arbitrary code execution.

## Impact
Successful exploitation may lead to a crash of the `sgitopnm` utility (Denial of Service) or arbitrary code execution in the context of the user executing the tool.

## Recommendation
- Inventory all systems utilizing Netpbm or libraries relying on `sgitopnm`.
- Update Netpbm to version 10.86.51, 11.02.29, 11.15.07, or later to address the vulnerability.
- Implement file integrity monitoring for high-risk input processing pipelines that utilize legacy image processing libraries.

objects.name: AWS EC2 Bulk User Data Enumeration
objects.description:
## Overview
